title: ICON 1.5 — The Character Sheet
description: A walk through the player character sheet, tab by tab. Needs a player character you own.

steps.title: Your character sheet
steps.content:
This tour opens your character sheet and walks through it tab by tab.
Nothing is changed on your character: the tour only shows where things are.

steps.title: Header
steps.content: Name, portrait, jobs (the primary job sets your class, base stats, traits and Limit Break), level and chapter. A brand-new character shows a Character Setup Wizard button here until it has a job.

steps.title: Quick Guide
steps.content: Opens the ICON Quick Guide: how a turn works, animated pictures of every area (blasts, bursts, lines, arcs, auras), the searchable glossary and an FAQ of edge cases.

steps.title: Tabs
steps.content: Narrative for life outside the fight, Combat for the tactical game, Conditions for statuses and saves, Relics & Trophies, and Notes with the character management tools.

steps.title: XP and Level Up
steps.content: Click the pips or use − / + to track XP. At 15 XP press Level Up: the wizard offers exactly the choices your new level gives (abilities, talents, masteries, relics, bond powers). The wand reopens the creation wizard for a level 0 character.

steps.title: Bond, Burdens, Ambitions, Gear
steps.content: Your Bond and its powers, Burdens and Ambitions (click a clock segment to fill it), Dust, Effort and Strain.

steps.title: Gear kits
steps.content: The basic adventurer's kit is always with you; tick the one kit of your bond you carry on this expedition (p.35). Click an item to mark it used, or to spend one use when it counts uses (Shift+click sets how many it has). New expedition restocks everything.

steps.title: Narrative Actions
steps.content: Your narrative actions and their ratings. Click an action's name to roll it: a dialog asks for difficulty and any extra dice, then the result goes to chat.

steps.title: HP, Vigor and class resources
steps.content: Hit points with wounds, Vigor (the temporary shield over HP) and the resources of your class, such as Vigilance, Blessing Tokens or Aether. A Seer's Great Wheel deck lives in Foundry's Cards: chat cards remind you when to draw, and each card in your hand has a Foretell button. The Seer's Great Wheel tour explains it.

steps.title: Power dice
steps.content: Every class can hold power dice, since many abilities and relics give one. + Die asks for a name, a size and a starting value; − / + tick it, rolls it, the cross discards it. They are all lost at the end of combat.

steps.title: Basic actions
steps.content: Attacks and actions every character has (p.85). rolls the attack against your targets; the range is shown as a reminder.

steps.title: Stats and saves
steps.content: Vitality, Defense, Speed, Armor, Fray and your damage die, worked out from your job and level. The save bar rolls a save (1d20, 10+).

steps.title: Equipped abilities
steps.content: Drag abilities into the slots (dropping on a full slot replaces it). Click one to open its panel below, double-click to open the item. The COMBO checkbox is your combo token: posting the base version of a combo ability ticks it, and while it is on, abilities marked as combos use their combo version. The lock protects talents, masteries and the remove buttons from accidental clicks during play.

steps.title: The ability panel
steps.content: The panel has a button for each thing the ability does: Attack Roll or Auto-Hit, Damage Roll, Show in Chat, and where they apply: the area (Small Blast, Line 5…) to place it on the map and target everyone inside · Mark target (one token targeted, range checked) and Track target (a reminder, not a mark) · Take stance · Infuse X to arm an infused version with Aether before rolling · Gamble · chips to drag a summon or an object onto the map, or to place spaces (pit, dangerous, motes…). With a combo token on and two combo versions, the first roll asks which one. Interrupts show their uses here (left/max), back at the start of your turn.

steps.title: Automated abilities
steps.content: Many abilities do part of the work for you. What the system can do appears as a button or chip in the ability's panel, or as a chat card at the right moment (start or end of a turn, end of a round, someone entering an area), with buttons for the statuses, saves and damage. Anything in the text with no button or card is yours to do by hand, as on paper. The Quick Guide FAQ has the same note.

steps.title: Limit Break and Resolve
steps.content: From level 2 your Limit Break lives here. Use Limit Break spends Resolve, any mix of your personal Resolve and the party pool (p.99) — the party pool is shared, so ask your team first.

steps.title: Damage Utility
steps.content: At the bottom of the tab: Damage Utility rolls damage that doesn't come from an ability's attack (a trait, a relic, an effect you are told to apply). Choose dice, fixed damage and modifiers, write the source, and the damage card has the usual Apply buttons.

steps.title: Conditions
steps.content: Click a status to apply or remove it; the ones marked auto change your rolls by themselves. Active negative statuses get a Save button here.

steps.title: Relics
steps.content: Drag relics here from the Relics compendium. Each card shows its rank and lets you upgrade it with Dust.

steps.title: Trophies
steps.content: Spoils taken from dungeons, factions and legends, with a limited number of uses; a character carries 3 at a time (p.242). Drag them from the Trophies compendium or make a + Custom trophy. Use spends a use and posts the trophy to chat; the checkboxes remind you of trophies in effect this combat or expedition. With no uses left a trophy crumbles.

steps.title: Character Management
steps.content: AP, masteries and skill ranks spent against what your levels have earned, with a warning if you overspend. Refocus refunds everything so you can rebuild; Guide reopens the character building guide.
